<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 18:7">Midr. Till. to Ps. XVIII, 2</cite> (expl. <he>ארחמך</he>, <cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 18:7">ib.</cite>) <he>רַחֲמִית יתך וכ׳</he> I love thee (ref. to Targ. Deut. l. c.); Yalk. ib. 671 <he>רַחְמָאִי יתך</he>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:3:8">Y. Ber. IX, 14ᵇ</cite> bot. (R. Akiba speaking to his pupils before his death) <he>רְחִמְתֵּיה בכל לבי ורחמתיה וכ׳</he> I loved him with all my heart, and I loved him with all I possessed, but how to love him with all my soul (life) I could not understand, and now &c.

<cite ref="Shabbat 23b:6">Sabb. 23ᵇ</cite> <he>דרָחֵים רבנן וכ׳</he> he who loves scholars shall have children that are scholars. Y. ib. XIV, 14ᵈ bot. <he>חד בר נש ר׳ אתתא וכ׳</he> a man fell in love with a woman … and grew dangerously ill; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 2:2:9">Y. Ab. Zar. II, 40ᵈ</cite> bot.

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 25:5">Lev. R. s. 25</cite> <he>שמעית דמלכא רַחְמָא וכ׳</he> I heard that the king loves figs; <cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 2:20:1">Koh. R. to II, 20</cite> <cite ref="T00499"><he>רחים</he></cite>; <cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 2:20:1">ib.</cite> <cite ref="T00500"><he>רחימא</he></cite>; <cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 2:20:1">ib.</cite> <he>רחמיה</he> (corr. acc.).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 2:3:7">Y. Ab. Zar. II, 41ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>דהוות רַחְמָא מצוותא</he> who loved to be charitable; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 8:3:8-9">Y. Ter. VIII, 45ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>הוו רחמנא וכ׳</he> (corr. acc.).
<cite ref="Ketubot 105b:7">Keth. 105ᵇ</cite> <he>אם מִרְחַם כולהו רַחְמוּ לי וכ׳</he> if there is love (among them), they all love me &c., v. <cite ref="O01224"><he>סְנֵי</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 89b:11">Snh. 89ᵇ</cite> <he>תרוייהו רַחֲמִינִי להו</he> I love both of them (Isaac und Ishmael); a. fr.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 103:13">Targ. Ps. CIII, 13</cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 28:13">Targ. Prov. XXVIII, 13</cite>; a. fr.
Targ. Gen. XXIX, 32 (O. ed. Vien. Pe.).

Targ. Y. Deut. VI, 5; a. e.—Keth. l. c. האי … דמְרַחְמִין ליה וכ׳ if the people of a place love a teacher, it is not because he is a good man, but because he does not reprove them on heavenly matters (for neglect of religious duties). Y. Ter. VIII, 45ᶜ אילולי דאתון מרחמין שמועתא וכ׳ but for your loving traditions (you would not ask such questions); is it not a Mishnah?; Y. Ab. Zar. II, 41ᵃ רחמין; a. e.—Trnsf. to give suck (v. preced.).
<cite ref="Bekhorot 24a:10">Bekh. 24ᵃ</cite> or shall we say, <he>דידה מְרַחְמָא דלא וכ׳</he> a dam gives suck to her own young, but not to a stranger.

<cite ref="Bekhorot 24a:10">Ib.</cite> <he>דילמא רַחוּמֵי רחים</he> perhaps this is a case when one gives suck to a stranger (although having a child of her own); v. <cite ref="U00169"><he>שְׁבַק</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Jeremiah 31:19">Targ. Jer. XXXI, 19</cite>.

<cite ref="Onkelos Deuteronomy 7:2">Targ. Deut. VII, 2</cite>; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Makkot 23b:17">Macc. 23ᵇ</cite> <he>מדהא מְרַחַמְתָּא והא לא מרחמתא</he> (Solomon found out which was the true mother of the living child,) because the one showed compassion, and the other did not. Y. Taan. II, 65ᵇ <he>אמרין … מִתְרַחֵם עלינן לינן מְרַחְמִין וכ׳</he> the men of Niniveh said, if thou wilt have no mercy on us, we shall have no mercy on them (the beasts and the children); a. fr.
